To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T cell colonies from human T cell depleted lymphocytes arise from contaminating T cells, not from pre-T cells.
the TCPC in PBM-E is not present in the E- fraction but is generated by the contaminating T cells in the E+ fraction.
The T colony progenitor frequency in T depleted peripheral blood monocytes (PBM-E-) is directly proportional to the amount of contaminating T lymphocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the T cell colony progenitor cell in T depleted human lymphocytes.
the analysis of human T lymphocytes in culture.
the origin of the T cell colonies which are generated in the limiting dilution assay of T depleted human lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCPC in PBM-E-, as in PBM-E+, is the mature T cell.
the TCPC in PBM-E-, as in PBM-E+, is a mature T cell which is not capable of self-renewal.
the TCPC is a mature T cell which is capable of rapidly expanding in culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TCPC in PBM-E-, is the T cell.
the TCPC frequency is low in the T cell depleted population and that the TCPC is not a pre-T cell.

T cells are not generated in culture from a pre-T cell in PBM-E-, but that the T cells which arise in culture are generated from contaminating T cells which are present at the outset of the experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TCPC in PBM-E-, as in PBM-E+, are T cells.
there is no pre-T population in PBM.
the TCPC in the T cell depleted population is not a pre-T cell but is rather a contaminating T cell.
